name: ui/notification-cascade
title: Notification cascade
desc_vi: Bốn thông báo điện thoại lần lượt rơi xuống, đẩy nhau lên; cả cụm bay đi rồi hiện thẻ kết có tiêu đề, logo và dòng chân.
params_vi: title: dòng đậm của mọi thông báo · messages: 4 dòng phụ · app_name, now_label, less_label, icon_letter (trống = biểu tượng bong bóng chat gốc), icon_from, icon_to: chữ và màu icon · headline_top, headline_accent, footer: thẻ kết · logo: ảnh logo trong suốt (đường dẫn) · bg_from, bg_mid, bg_to: nền · end_ink, end_accent: màu chữ thẻ kết
notes: Portrait design 1080 x 1920: the block builds the design at those pixels and fits it (contain, centred) to the target box with one static CSS scale (1 in a 1080 x 1920 film; 0.5625 in the 608 x 1080 demo slot), so every size and tween value is the source pixel value. Timings, pitch (214 px), eases and colours as in the source. Differences: the backdrop photograph (a desk photo, unclear licence) is a generated warm gradient (bg_from / bg_mid / bg_to) with the same slow push-in; the HyperFrames logo on the end card is an image param (default: a generated neutral mark, ui-logo-light.png in demo-assets); end-card headline font Georgia bold serif -> the film's font bold (no system fonts in films), font = the film's font everywhere else (source: -apple-system / Helvetica Neue); texts are params with Vietnamese defaults (NOW -> BÂY GIỜ, Show less -> Thu gọn); the 14 s composition length is the demo duration; the source's section wrappers (data-start 1.59 / 9.89) are not needed because the tweens carry the timing. Imitates the iOS notification centre (brand_ui). 05/10/2026: the source's own assets are back as defaults (user's decision: open-source assets are used as shipped); pass a param to use your own. Banner app icon: the source's own 100 px green gradient squircle (#5ae458 -> #1fc83f, radius 24) with the white speech-bubble glyph (64 x 60 SVG at left 18, top 20) is the default; set `icon_letter` to a letter to get a one-letter mark instead, `icon_from` / `icon_to` for other colours.
